reachable: YES — fully live at the scored read position, and it gets gradient there. The chase reads cmd_raw = tok_emb[:,0::2] and obs_mem = tok_emb[:,1::2] with allowed = (pair_j < cmd_i) AND (valid_obs_j AND valid_cmd_j). Nothing references the CURRENT step's observation, so the "gated on an observation that is absent at the read" failure does not apply. Under the exact cups layout (cups_probe.build_cups_layout: L odd, read command alone at rpos=2r, all prior cmd/obs valid, batch padded to Lmax), n_pair = r and every pair 0..r-1 is allowed at the read command, i.e. the full prefix is visible. I ran the real genome through evolve.genome.load_arch, woke the zero-init readout, and the prediction delta at rpos is nonzero for rows with r=3,4,6 (7.65 / 6.51 / 5.90) while remaining exactly 0.0 at obs positions and at every position after the read. Perturbing an earlier COMMAND embedding changes the read-position prediction (delta 4.36) — the differential channel comp_ca pays for. With the readout nonzero, a loss taken only at the read positions gives nonzero gradient to every chase parameter. The head wrap (r18_transition_forwardmodel_consistency) leaves the channel active and finite. In training the layout is the same alternation (baseline_interleave, CUPS_LAYOUT="interleave2"), and collate clearing cmd+obs together never produces a cmd-present/obs-absent pair, so `allowed` is never spuriously false there.
solves_outside_model: NO. The impl is 188 lines of pure tensor code over tok_emb/types/key_pad. There is no string parsing anywhere, no Python-side resolution of the move chain, nothing written into the command token. Addresses are learned projections of the frozen 768-d command embeddings; the retrieval is a masked softmax over strictly-earlier steps. The hop-0 query is the READ command's own source address, and the read command is byte-identical between the native and role-swapped arms, so the entire differential comes from the mv command embeddings — exactly the quantity the objective pays for, not a re-encoding of the answer. This is not the shape of the prior retraction. I also confirmed the mechanism is structurally position-blind in its content selection: attention scores are cosine over addresses derived from command embeddings only, with no positional term, so it cannot cheaply degenerate into the first-mover / move-order-position lookup that the analytic band shows scores positive on this frozen slice (h_first +0.1685). Position enters only through h_cmd in the halting mixture and the output gate, which reweight candidates it has already selected by address.
summary: The code implements exactly the mechanism the hypothesis describes, and I confirmed it functionally rather than by reading. Installing hand-made address heads (src/dst = controlled one-hots) and reading out each hop's candidate content at the read position: on a depth-3 chain P0->X->Y->Z with content A exposed at P0, hops 0-2 return the constant mv observation and hop 3 returns A (cos 1.0); on the role-swapped chain over the same board with the same read command, hop 3 returns B; on a depth-4 chain, hop 4 returns A. That is a genuine iterated backward resolution — query = the read location's address, each hop matches DESTINATION addresses of strictly-earlier steps, reads the paired observation as that hop's candidate, and replaces the query with the matched step's SOURCE address — resolving depth d at hop d, with a 6-hop budget covering the eligible slice (depths 3 and 4). Every structural claim checks out: two-layer GELU trunk, n_addr=2 unit-normalized (64,256) head pairs, cosine summed over channels with one learned temperature (chase_logit_scale, clamped 0.5-64), gated query transition, halting logits over [h_cmd, 32-d content projection, sharpness, RMS, cosine to a learned null direction, hop embedding], softmax mixture, zero-init (D,D) readout under a sigmoid gate. Forward is bit-identical to the parent r22 at init in both eval and train mode. Muon takes the four (64,256) address heads (shape count 4 >= 2, so the sibling rule fires), the spectral cap takes chase_out.weight. Cost 1.29x forward, 1.22x fwd+bwd — the stated ~1.3x. The genome differs from the parent on the arch axis only; every other axis matches r3-06-within-sequence-contrast exactly. The data claims are also right: mv steps have output "" so render_obs yields the near-constant "cwd=... exit=0\n", routing lives only in the mv command text, and "n=89 (d3 60, d4+ 29)" is quoted from the BRIEF and matches research/compositional-selection-design.md's 89 inner windows at depths {3,4}. One worry I had — that hop 0 would collide between the read slot's own exposure and a later mv into it — is unfounded on this data: every mv destination is a freshly suffixed path with exactly one writer, and the read path is never an exposure slot, so the backward chain is unambiguous. Two divergences, both minor and both about the hypothesis's claimed *verification* rather than its mechanism: "gradients reach every new parameter" is false at initialization (only chase_out.{weight,bias} get gradient; 21 upstream params get exactly zero until the zero-init readout departs from zero), and the whole "What I did verify locally" block was asserted without torch — I reproduced all of it except that item. WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: (1) the author's own #1 risk — whether the frozen encoder's mean-pooled `mv A B` embedding retains a linearly recoverable src/dst asymmetry so the two heads can separate; that needs the real encoder and data. (2) Related and worse on this data than the hypothesis admits: the destination paths within a window differ only by a numeric suffix (sshd_config.cfg.6 vs .7 vs .8), so the dst head must discriminate near-identical mean-pooled strings; the hypothesis's "address collision" bullet covers the ~20-unrelated-paths case but not this near-duplicate case. (3) Whether the halting softmax explores past hop 0 inside the fixed step budget, and whether the readout bootstrap leaves enough steps for the 6-hop stack to converge. (4) The actual comp_ca — no training was run. I modified nothing in the repo; scratch scripts are at /tmp/rev-slot00/t3.py, /tmp/rev-slot00/t4.py, /tmp/rev-slot00/t5.py; no packages installed.

divergences.claim: "gradients reach every new parameter" (hypothesis line 91, listed under "What I did verify locally")
divergences.what_the_code_does: At initialization only chase_out.weight and chase_out.bias receive gradient. All 21 upstream chase parameters — chase_ln, chase_in, chase_mid, chase_src.{0,1}, chase_dst.{0,1}, chase_content, chase_hop_emb, chase_null, chase_logit_scale, chase_step_gate, chase_halt, chase_gate — get EXACTLY zero gradient, because contrib = gate * chase_out(mixed) and chase_out.weight is zero-init, so d(contrib)/d(mixed) = 0 and d(contrib)/d(gate) = 0. They only receive gradient once the readout departs from zero (which it does, since chase_out.weight is in the AdamW `rest` group and its own gradient is nonzero). Verified: loss at the read position with the readout at init -> 21 zero-grad chase params; after perturbing chase_out.weight -> 0 zero-grad chase params. Same bootstrap pattern as the parent's zero-init x_out, so the mechanism is trainable; the literal claim is false at step 0 and the address trunk / halting stack learns nothing until the readout wakes up, which compounds the author's own listed "halting softmax collapses onto one hop early" risk.
